# 7-day sample menu: after a kidney transplant

--8<-- "includes/starting-points.md"

With a working transplant, most people no longer need the strict kidney diet. KDIGO asks transplant recipients to follow a healthy lifestyle with a proper diet, and your transplant team sets your own numbers. This week uses the app's stage 1–2 starting points: 56–70 g of protein for a 70 kg adult and sodium under 2,000 mg. Three things are different after a transplant. **Food safety:** anti-rejection medicines weaken the immune system, so every meat, fish and egg is cooked through and there is no deli meat or smoked fish. **No grapefruit or its relatives,** which change the blood level of some anti-rejection medicines. **Glucose:** steroids and tacrolimus can raise it, so carbohydrate stays at about 55 g a meal and your team adjusts insulin. Potassium is shown because tacrolimus can raise it; follow your blood tests.

## The numbers this menu is built to

Built for a reference adult: 70 kg, 170 cm, type 1 diabetes, using the app's starting targets for **after a transplant (the stage 1–2 starting points)** (see [Eating well](../index.md#your-numbers)). Every day below was checked against these numbers by `scripts/build_handbook.py`.

| Per day | Built to |
|---|---|
| Protein | 56–70 g (0.8–1.0 g/kg) |
| Sodium | at most 2,000 mg |
| Potassium | no limit (shown for information) |
| Phosphorus | no limit (shown for information) |
| Energy from food | 1,750–2,450 kcal |
| Carbohydrate | about 55 g at each main meal (every meal 50–60 g); snacks 10–30 g |

Also: no foods with phosphate additives; no grapefruit, pomelo or Seville orange (they change the blood levels of some transplant medicines); no foods that need extra care with a weakened immune system (smoked fish, deli meats, hot dogs, raw shellfish); everything is cooked through.

## Swaps that keep the numbers

- **Fruit:** any fruit except grapefruit, pomelo, Seville orange and tangelo. Oranges, clementines, berries, apples, pears and canned fruit in juice are all fine.
- **Protein foods:** chicken, turkey, pork, beef, fish and eggs swap ounce for ounce, always cooked to a safe temperature (poultry 165 °F, fish and whole cuts 145 °F).
- **Cheese:** hard cheese such as cheddar is fine. Soft cheeses are safe only if the label says they are made from pasteurized milk.
- **Grains:** whole-wheat bread, brown rice and oatmeal swap with their white versions at the same carbohydrate.

## Make it yours

- **Scale for your weight.** Protein here is 0.8–1.0 g per kg for 70 kg: 48–60 g a day at 60 kg and 64–80 g at 80 kg. Ask your transplant dietitian which weight and range to use.
- **If your potassium runs high,** your team may ask you to limit it; the [stage 3 menu](g3.md) shows lower-potassium days.
- **Glucose changes after a transplant.** Steroids and tacrolimus can raise glucose. Check as your team asks and report highs and lows; never change insulin on your own.
- **Carbohydrate stays steady:** about the same amount at each main meal every day, so a fixed insulin plan or a carbohydrate ratio works the same way from day to day. Your own amount per meal comes from your diabetes team; keep it consistent and count what you actually eat ([Carb counting](../carb-counting.md)).
- **Lows come first.** Treat a low straight away with glucose tablets or another fast 15 g ([Treating a low](../../t1d/treating-a-low.md)), even if it adds potassium or fluid. Rescue foods are on top of these menus and are never "against the rules".
- **Hungry, or losing weight without trying?** Add calories with olive oil, unsalted butter or more measured starch covered by your usual insulin plan, not with more meat, and tell your dietitian ([Eating enough](../eating-enough.md)).
- **Season without salt:** herbs, spices, garlic and onion powder, lemon and vinegar. Do not use salt substitutes: they contain potassium chloride ([Sodium](../sodium.md)).
- **Log it in the app:** every food here is in the app's food list under the same name. Saved meals and "copy day" let you reuse a menu day ([Planning and menus](../../app/planning-and-menus.md)).

## Sources

- [USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)][FDC]: every nutrient value, through the app's food list.
- [KDIGO 2009 transplant recipient guideline][K09TX]: a healthy lifestyle with exercise and a proper diet (Rec 26).
- [KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline][K24]: sodium under 2 g a day (Rec 3.3.2.1).
- [USDA–FDA: food safety for transplant recipients][FSTX], [FoodSafety.gov: weakened immune systems][FOODSAFE] and [FoodSafety.gov: safe minimum internal temperatures][FSTEMPS]: deli meats, smoked fish and raw shellfish; safe cooking temperatures.
- [FDA: grapefruit juice and some drugs don't mix][FDAgrapefruit]; [Prograf (tacrolimus) label][PROGRAF]: avoid grapefruit; tacrolimus can raise glucose and potassium.
- [ADA Standards of Care 2026, section 5][A26-5]: consistent carbohydrate in time and amount for people on fixed insulin plans (Rec 5.28).
- [NKF: carbohydrate counting with CKD][DG7]: 15 g is one carbohydrate choice; 3–6 choices per meal, set by your dietitian.
